messages:
sarah_support: FYI ACME Enterprise reports a pattern of SSE streams dropping mid-response. Users get partial JSON, then the client reconnects and sometimes sees duplicate output. They're seeing billing for the partial + resumed tokens.

acme_it_julia: This only happens for users behind our corporate proxy + VPN. Firewall logs show a TLS renegotiation / client-cert request right before the reset.

devin_eng: Can you paste a short client console log + any server access log snippet? Browser/os/library used?

sarah_support: Repro from one user: Windows 10, Chrome 118, internal SSO extension that injects a client cert. Client console: 
```
EventSource failed: Error connecting to https://api.redwood.example/stream?v=abc status: 0
fetch error: net::ERR_CONNECTION_RESET
partial chunk received: {\"choices\":[{\"delta\":{\"content\":\"Here's the first part...\"}}]\n```

acme_it_julia: Firewall snippet: 
```
2024-11-02T14:03:21Z paloalto[proxy]: tls renegotiate request from 10.10.10.1 -> 34.56.78.90:443, client-cert-ask
2024-11-02T14:03:21Z paloalto[proxy]: sent FIN to client, reset stream id 12
```

ryan_oncall: On our ingress (nginx) we see upstream closed mid-stream: 
```
[14/Nov/2024:14:03:21 +0000] "GET /stream?v=abc HTTP/1.1" 499 0 "-" "Mozilla/5.0" upstream_response_time: 3.422
error: recv() failed (104: Connection reset by peer)
```

devin_eng: Diagnosis: TLS renegotiation / client-cert prompt from the middlebox is tearing down the TLS session. SSE/chunked HTTP/1.1 streams often don't survive a mid-connection rehandshake on many corporate proxies. Two immediate asks: 1) quick customer workaround, 2) long-term mitigations.

alan_netops: We can repro in lab. Palo Alto will send a ClientCertRequest if it thinks it needs to re-auth the client. It effectively forces a TLS rehandshake which ends the existing TCP/TLS session. Best short-term: disable SSL-decrypt / client-cert inspection for api.redwood.example or whitelist the path.

sarah_support: Suggested minimal repro steps for eng to reproduce locally: 
```
# run mitmproxy to simulate corporate SSL-inspection that requests certs
mitmproxy --mode regular --ssl-insecure
# then from a client force HTTP/1.1 streaming keep-alive
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/stream?v=test"
# while open, trigger proxy to request client cert or use openssl s_client -reconnect to simulate renegotiation
```

devin_eng: Potential mitigations: 
- Short-term: ask customer to whitelist/ bypass SSL-inspection for /stream endpoints. That's the fastest fix.
- Short-term (server): add a server-side note to detect early FIN/ECONNRESET and surface a specific support message so we can quickly issue credits.
- Medium-term: implement resumable streaming semantics (stream-id + byte/seq offset) so clients can resume without double-billing; server dedupes partial output.
- Docs: add corporate-proxy troubleshooting guide for SSE (headers to check, mitmproxy repro).

sarah_support: Is there a safe header customers can set to reduce MITM behavior (e.g., to hint no-transform)? Will proxies honor it?

alan_netops: "Cache-Control: no-transform" is occasionally respected but not reliable for corporate middleboxes that do deep inspection. The only reliable approach is whitelist rules on the proxy or disable client-cert requests for that virtual-host/path.

devin_eng: For a very short-term customer-facing mitigation we're adding an optional header X-Stream-Bypass which our edge can echo; document will recommend customers add it and ask their netops team to whitelist requests with that header. Not perfect, but easier than changing all customers' firewall configs. @deploy_bot can we canary this on staging?

deploy_bot: deploy plan created: roll x-stream-bypass header to staging tomorrow 03:00 UTC. Monitor metrics for 1h, then decide prod rollout.

acme_it_julia: We'll open an internal ticket with our netops to whitelist api.redwood.example/stream and run tests tomorrow. We'll capture a pcap of the failure window and send it to support.

sarah_support: Please include exact user timestamps and client IPs. We'll correlate with our ingress logs and prepare credits for impacted sessions.

devin_eng: Follow-ups for eng: prototype resumable stream session id + server-side dedupe, add guard/error message for 499/resets to speed support triage, and docs for corporate proxy troubleshooting.

ryan_oncall: Noted — I'll prepare a billing reconciliation workflow for truncated streams and coordinate credits.

sarah_support: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for tracking. :pray:
